text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
White sugar futures in London closed higher on trade buying and short covering. August last traded at $321.50 per tonne, up $2.10, while October ended 30 cents higher at $315.50 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed an active session weaker as speculators continued to roll spot July contracts into the back months ahead of the first notice day. July futures expire on June 30. July lost 19 points to close at 10.92 cents/lb. October lost 11 points to close at 11.14 cents/lb. The fall should not have come as a surprise against the background of abundant supplies.

SINGAPORE - Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 5,225 tonnes, raw value, compared to 5,325 tonnes in February 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first two months of 1997 (January/February) up to 37,852 tonnes compared to 31,564 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1996 hit the record high of 313,726 tonnes against 271,334 tonnes in 1995. Major countries of origin January/February 1997 were Australia with 21,324 tonnes raws against nil and Malaysia with 6,781 tonnes whites compared to 8,487 tonnes.

Sugar exports in January/February 1997 amounted to 4,625 tonnes compared to 3,071 tonnes in 1996. Total exports in 1996 reached 11,148 tonnes against 22,136 tonnes in 1995. The major country of destination in January/February 1997 was Vietnam with 3,000 tonnes against nil.

POLAND - Sugar imports in March 1997 reached 11,498 tonnes, raw value, up from 2,427 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996/97 (September/March) up to 65,396 tonnes against 70,685 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 were 85,306 tonnes against 100,248 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were the UK with 24,326 tonnes whites against nil and Germany with 16,865 tonnes compared to 10,132 tonnes.

Sugar exports in March 1997 amounted to 7,734 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in September/March 1996/97 up to 200,330 tonnes against 2,264 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 4,440 tonnes against 14,828 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Germany with 23,569 tonnes whites against nil, Algeria with 23,279 tonnes against nil, Syria with 28,189 tonnes raws against nil and Algeria with 18,450 tonnes compared to 288 tonnes.

DENMARK - The weather in the week ended June 22 was very changeable with temperatures around the long term mean. Cumulative rains since April 1 ranged between 90 and 162 mm compared to the long term average of 116-124 mm. Growth is considered to be very good and farmers reported the closing of the rows. Growers have started to weed mechanically. There are no diseases and only scattered aphids attacks.

Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) issued a tender to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raws. Both cargoes are for delivery in August, with July 15 set as the final date to receive price offers. Results will be announced on July 16. GEZA said the tender replaces the one cancelled earlier in June.
